ledger.note: 1692: Emperor Leopold I elevates Duke Ernest Augustus of Calenberg to elector, creating the Electorate of Hanover. Infobox 'Elevation to Electorate: 1692'; 'the elevation did not become official until the approval of' the Imperial Diet in 1708 (infobox 'Electorate formally approved: 1708'). The page names the principalities and counties but gives no boundary.

region.text: the Principality of Lüneburg (Celle), inherited on the death of Duke George William

ledger.note: 1705: George Louis inherits Lüneburg. 'In 1705, Elector George I Louis inherited the Principality of Lüneburg with the Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg upon the death' of Duke George William (infobox 'Inherited Lüneburg and Saxe-Lauenburg: 1705'); the page also names the principality of Celle.

region.text: the Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg, inherited with Lüneburg

ledger.note: 1705: Saxe-Lauenburg comes with Lüneburg. Same sentence as the Lüneburg event. The Bremen-Verden page adds that Emperor Charles VI enfeoffed George II with Saxe-Lauenburg in 1728 (the Electorate page: 'In 1728, Emperor Charles VI officially enfeoffed George II'); a legal confirmation, not a second gain.

ledger.note: 1715: Hanover takes Bremen-Verden from the Danes. Denmark-Norway, which had occupied the Swedish duchies in 1712, 'sold to him Bremen-Verden' (George I) in 1715 in return for his aid against Sweden, and Hanover 'took de facto possession'; Sweden did not cede it until 1719. The page gives no day or month for the possession, so the start year is read from the sale.

ledger.note: 1719: the Treaty of Stockholm gives Hanover Bremen-Verden. 'Hanover acquired Bremen-Verden in 1719' (infobox 'Acquired Bremen-Verden: 1715'). The Bremen-Verden page: Hanover owed Sweden 1 million rixdollars; the page says it took until 1733 before the emperor also enfeoffed George II with the duchies. Cliopatria draws the land from 1721.

region.text: the Land of Hadeln (311.6 km2), on the Elbe-Weser coast

ledger.note: 1731: Hanover gains Hadeln. 'In 1731, Hanover also gained Hadeln.' The page does not name the former holder; the Bremen-Verden page says Bremen-Verden received its administration 'through a redeployment of Hanoverian territories', so the counterpart is the Cliopatria aggregate that holds the minor estates. Below the shape's resolution (about 1.5 cells).

region.text: the electorate, invaded by the French in summer 1757

ledger.note: 1757: the French invade Hanover and win at Hastenbeck. 'The Battle of Hastenbeck (26 July 1757)'; the infobox has 'French forces occupy the Electorate of Hanover'. The Electorate page: 'In the summer of 1757, the French invaded Hanover and defeated' the Duke of Cumberland. The page dates the battle, not the zone.

region.text: the electorate, after the Convention of Klosterzeven

ledger.note: 1757: the Convention of Klosterzeven halts the fighting. The Klosterzeven page: 'signed on 10 September 1757' and the army 'must withdraw across the Elbe into the Duchy of Lauenburg' with a garrison of 4,000 to 6,000 men left in Stade; the Electorate and Hastenbeck pages give 18 September. The convention was later revoked and Hanover 're-entered the war the following year'.

region.text: the electorate, partly occupied by French forces after the convention

ledger.note: 1757: the French occupy Hanover. The Hastenbeck page says the battle 'resulted in the Convention of Klosterzeven' and 'the occupation of Hanover'; the Klosterzeven page calls it a 'partial occupation by French forces' without naming the districts.

1758: the French are expelled. 'The following year' British, Prussian, Hessian and Brunswick troops 'again expelled the occupants'; 'Hanover was unaffected for the rest of the war'. The Minden page: 'in 1758, a counter-offensive commanded by Ferdinand saw French forces first driven back across the Rhine'. No month on either page.

region.text: the electorate, occupied by 24,000 Prussian soldiers

ledger.note: 1801: Prussia occupies Hanover. 'In 1801, there was an invasion of 24,000 Prussian soldiers that surprised Hanover, which surrendered without a fight'; they arrived at Stade in April.

region.text: the electorate, evacuated by the Prussians

ledger.note: 1801: the Prussians leave. After arriving at Stade 'in April', they 'stayed there until October'.

region.text: the electorate's last Cliopatria shape, 31,786 km2

ledger.note: 1802: Cliopatria's electorate row ends and its 'Kingdom of Hanover' row (1803-1865) takes the same realm. The year is Cliopatria's, not the page's: the Electorate page dates the acquisition of Osnabrück to 25 February 1803, the French invasion to 26 May 1803 and the Convention of Artlenburg to 5 July 1803, and the infobox ends the electorate in 1807 (Westphalia) with the kingdom re-established in 1814.

wars.outcome: Denmark-Norway occupied Bremen-Verden in 1712 and sold it to George I in 1715; Hanover took de facto possession and Sweden ceded it in the 1719 Treaty of Stockholm for 1 million rixdollars.
wars.note: Only the Bremen-Verden episode is covered; the page does not date the war itself.

wars.name: Seven Years' War

zones.text: the electorate, invaded by the French in summer 1757

wars.outcome: The French defeated the Anglo-Hanoverian army at Hastenbeck (26 July 1757) and occupied Hanover after the Convention of Klosterzeven (September 1757); the convention was disavowed and the French expelled in 1758; at Minden (1 August 1759) 'the battle ended all French designs upon Hanover for the remainder of the year'. No change of Hanoverian territory.
wars.note: The pages opened end with Minden (1759); later campaigns and the treaty year are not on them. The Electorate page says Hanover was 'unaffected for the rest of the war' after 1758. The Minden page records the French capture of Minden on 10 July 1759.

wars.name: Prussian occupation of Hanover (1801)

zones.text: the electorate, occupied from April to October 1801

wars.outcome: 24,000 Prussian soldiers occupied the electorate without a fight and stayed until October 1801; no change of ownership.
wars.note: The page links the move to Prussia joining the pro-French coalition of armed neutral powers; no article of that name was opened.

certainty.note: No page opened gives boundary lines; the electorate was a patchwork (the page lists Calenberg, Grubenhagen, Lüneburg, Diepholz, Hoya, Saxe-Lauenburg, Bremen-Verden, Hadeln) drawn as Cliopatria's generalised shape. The Bremen-Verden frontier follows the 1719 treaty but the page gives no line; only the 1803 areas of Bremen (5,325.4 km2) and Verden (1,359.7 km2).

notes: START: Cliopatria's row begins 1709; the dossier starts in 1692 (elevation, infobox) with new keyframes for 1692-1704 and 1705-1708 whose lands are named from the page (Calenberg with Göttingen, Grubenhagen, Diepholz, Hoya; then Lüneburg and Saxe-Lauenburg in 1705) and not yet in the gazetteer. The Diet approved the elevation in 1708. END: Cliopatria ends the electorate in 1802 and begins a 'Kingdom of Hanover' row (Q164079, 1803-1865) in 1803. Both are the same Hanoverian realm under the same dynasty and capital (the page: electorate merged into Westphalia 1807, kingdom re-established 1814); the dissolve event is therefore Cliopatria's boundary, at confidence 1. The orchestrator should give kingdom-of-hanover the electorate's colour (family germany). Osnabrück (25 February 1803, real union), the French invasion (26 May 1803), the Convention of Artlenburg (5 July 1803), the Prussian and Russo-British-Swedish episodes of 1805-1806 and Westphalia (1807, 1810) belong to the kingdom's dossier. PERSONAL UNION: the page puts the personal union with Great Britain and Ireland at 1714 (the body says it lasted until 1837, the infobox 1807); no territory changes, so no ledger event; Britain's dossier may record it. KEYFRAMES: the 1757-1761 and 1762 shapes are verdict wrong (62 cells of unexplained land, no acquisition on the page; probably the war theatre); the 1763-1802 shapes are adjusted to remove Osnabrück, which Cliopatria draws from 1763 although the page gives real union only in 1803; the page says Osnabrück was ruled by every second ruler of the House of Hanover since 1662 and does not date those terms, so a gap-filler should open 'Prince-Bishopric of Osnabrück'. Bremen-Verden is drawn from 1721 by Cliopatria but 1719 on the page (and held from 1715 as an occupation). DISAGREEMENTS: Klosterzeven signed 10 September 1757 (Klosterzeven page) against 18 September (Electorate and Hastenbeck pages); Bremen-Verden acquired 1715 or 1719 (the Electorate page has both: purchase 1715, treaty 1719); union with Britain 1807 against 1837. The Electorate page gives no area. NOT COVERED (page budget, five pages): the 1760-1762 campaigns, whether the Danes held Bremen-Verden until 1715 in Cliopatria's Denmark-Norway row, and the dates of the Hanoverian prince-bishops of Osnabrück. GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: Principality of Calenberg (with Göttingen), Principality of Grubenhagen, County of Diepholz, County of Hoya, Principality of Lüneburg (Celle), Duchy of Saxe-Lauenburg, Land Hadeln; Bremen-Verden is written as the difference of Cliopatria's 1721 and 1713 shapes (27 cells) so it draws today, and a gazetteer entry 'Bremen-Verden' (the duchies between Elbe and Weser, Stade, about 6,700 km2) would let a later pass replace that. COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: principality-of-calenberg, principality-of-luneburg and duchy-of-saxe-lauenburg (the eu-09-d report also asks for the last two), prince-bishopric-of-osnabruck, kingdom-of-hanover (a Cliopatria row, group unknown). The native names are the standard German forms, not read from a page. Quoted fragments are the page text as WebFetch returned it (a small model reads the page); the Electorate page was re-read with verbatim prompts for every dated sentence used.
